questions.question: The Trilateral Highway Project aims to enhance connectivity between India and which two Southeast Asian countries?
questions.questionHtml: The Trilateral Highway Project aims to enhance connectivity between India and which two Southeast Asian countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Myanmar and Thailand.

Key Points

  • The Trilateral Highway Project is a strategic initiative aimed at enhancing connectivity between India, Myanmar, and Thailand.
  • This highway spans approximately 1,360 km, connecting Moreh in Manipur, India, to Mae Sot in Thailand via Myanmar.
  • It facilitates trade, cultural exchange, and economic cooperation between India and Southeast Asian nations as part of India’s "Act East Policy."
  • The project is jointly developed by India, Myanmar, and Thailand to improve transportation infrastructure in the region.
  • India has invested significantly in road construction in Myanmar under this project, including the Kalewa-Yagyi section and upgrading 69 bridges along the route.

Additional Information

  • Bangladesh and Bhutan

    • Bhutan is connected to India through bilateral agreements and road networks.
  • Nepal and Bhutan

  • NASA often collaborates with international space agencies, such as ISRO, to contribute scientific payloads for space exploration missions.

questions.solution: UV and X-ray absorption during solar storms causes a temperature increase in the thermosphere. questions.question: A shopkeeper marked an item 50% above its cost price. He then offered two successive discounts of 10% and 20% to a customer. If he made a profit of ₹80, at what price did he sell the item to that customer?
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper marked an item 50% above its cost price. He then offered two successive discounts of 10% and 20% to a customer. If he made a profit of ₹80, at what price did he sell the item to that customer?
questions.solution:
Let Cost Price = 100

⇒ Marked Price = 100 × 150 ÷ 100 = 150

⇒ After 10% discount = 150 × 90 ÷ 100 = 135

⇒ After 20% discount = 135 × 80 ÷ 100 = 108

⇒ Profit on CP 100 = 108 − 100 = 8

⇒ If profit 8 corresponds to 80, So 1 corresponds to 10

⇒ Required Selling Price = 108 × 10 = 1080

questions.question: A is three times as efficient as a worker than B, which allows A to complete a job in 60 days less than B. If they work together, they can finish the job in:
questions.questionHtml: A is three times as efficient as a worker than B, which allows A to complete a job in 60 days less than B. If they work together, they can finish the job in:
questions.solution:
Efficiency of A : B = 3 : 1 ⇒ Time of A : Time of B = 1 : 3.

Let Time of A = x, Time of B = 3x ⇒ 3x − x = 60 ⇒ 2x = 60 ⇒ x = 30.

Time of A = 30 days, Time of B = 90 days ⇒ Total work = LCM(30, 90) = 90 units.

Rate of A = 90 ÷ 30 = 3 units/day, Rate of B = 90 ÷ 90 = 1 unit/day ⇒ Combined rate = 3 + 1 = 4 units/day.

Time together = 90 ÷ 4 = 22.5 days.

⇒ Speed = 64 ÷ 4.8 = 13.33 km/h

questions.question: A vertical pole of height H stands on the ground. From a point P on the ground, the angle of elevation of the top of the pole is 60°. From a different point Q, located 10 meters away from point P (directly along the line extending from the base of the pole), the angle of elevation to the top of the pole is 30°.What is the height of the pole?
questions.questionHtml: A vertical pole of height H stands on the ground. From a point P on the ground, the angle of elevation of the top of the pole is 60°. From a different point Q, located 10 meters away from point P (directly along the line extending from the base of the pole), the angle of elevation to the top of the pole is 30°.What is the height of the pole?
questions.solution:
Let distance of P from pole = x

⇒ tan 60º = H ÷ x ⇒ √3 = H ÷ x ⇒ H = x√3

⇒ tan 30º = H ÷ (x + 10) ⇒ 1 ÷ √3 = H ÷ (x + 10) ⇒ H = (x + 10) ÷ √3

⇒ x√3 = (x + 10) ÷ √3 ⇒ x × 3 = x + 10 ⇒ 3x = x + 10 ⇒ 2x = 10 ⇒ x = 5

⇒ H = 5√3

questions.questionHtml:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph:
1. A key strategy is to diversify energy sources, transitioning from fossil fuels to renewable alternatives like solar, wind, and geothermal power.
2. To mitigate the worst effects of climate change, the global community must drastically reduce its reliance on carbon-intensive energy production.
3. This shift not only decreases greenhouse gas emissions but also improves air quality and creates new economic opportunities.
4. Additionally, policies that promote energy efficiency in buildings and transportation can further lower overall energy consumption.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: 2, 1, 3, 4.

Sentence 2 introduces the problem (climate change mitigation requires reducing carbon-intensive energy). Sentence 1 provides a key strategy (diversifying energy sources to renewables). Sentence 3 explains the benefits of this shift (reduced emissions, better air, economic opportunities). Finally, Sentence 4 adds supplementary measures (energy efficiency in buildings and transportation). Each sentence logically builds on the previous one.
